title: Asset Management and Investment Fund Regulation: International Edition
summary: A ten-module programme mapping asset management and fund regulation through IOSCO and FSB standards, from fund regimes and delegation to liquidity, cross-border distribution, sustainability and resilience.
intro: This training programme equips supervisors and industry practitioners to navigate asset management and fund regulation through international standards: classifying funds and managers, and assessing delegation, depositaries, liquidity, cross-border distribution, sustainability disclosures and operational resilience.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give supervisors and practitioners a clear map of how funds, their managers and their distribution are regulated around the world, anchored in IOSCO principles and FSB recommendations. Participants leave able to determine which type of regime applies to a given structure, test arrangements for delegation, custody, liquidity, leverage and valuation, and anticipate how authorities are likely to approach them.
sections.What It Covers: The asset management value chain and regulatory perimeter, the international standard-setting architecture, retail, professional and alternative fund regimes, manager authorisation, delegation and substance, distribution and investor disclosure, depositaries and custody, liquidity management tools, leverage and valuation, cross-border passporting and mutual recognition, sustainability disclosure and greenwashing, and operational resilience and emerging fund models.
Intended Audience: Supervisors, authorisation and policy staff at securities and markets authorities covering funds and asset managers
Compliance, legal, risk and product staff at fund managers, investment managers, distributors and fund platforms
Directors, depositary, custody and fund administration staff who need a working map of fund regulation across jurisdictions
Learning Objectives: Explain how fund regulation is organised internationally and determine which type of regime applies across the value chain
Distinguish product-regulated retail funds from manager-regulated professional and alternative fund regimes
Assess manager authorisation, delegation, substance and depositary arrangements against international standards
Evaluate liquidity management tools, leverage and valuation and what can go wrong
Apply the principles of fair distribution, investor disclosure, cross-border recognition and sustainability claims
Identify how operational resilience, supervisory convergence and new fund models are reshaping the sector
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day workshops. Each module combines a technical briefing with comparative case studies and break-out exercises, and modules can be selected or tailored for supervisors, managers or distributors.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of asset management, funds or their supervision is helpful. No legal background or knowledge of any particular jurisdiction's rules is required.
Core Reading: IOSCO, Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation (2017)
FSB, Revised Policy Recommendations to Address Structural Vulnerabilities from Liquidity Mismatch in Open-Ended Funds (2023)
IOSCO, Recommendations on Sustainability-Related Practices, Policies, Procedures and Disclosure in Asset Management (2021)
IOSCO, Thematic Analysis: Emerging Risks in Private Finance (2023)

modules.title: The Asset Management Value Chain and Regulatory Perimeter
modules.summary: Level-setting on investing, asset management and collective investment, who does what across the value chain, and a framework for deciding where the regulatory perimeter falls for a given activity or structure.
objectives: Explain what asset management and collective investment schemes are and why investors use them
Map the value chain from product design and distribution to management, custody and administration
Determine which activities fall inside the perimeter by asking what, who and how
syllabus: Collective investment versus segregated mandates and wealth management
Fund vehicles: corporate, contractual, trust and partnership structures
Activities, entities and products as three lenses on regulation
Break-out: placing a fund structure inside the regulatory perimeter

modules.title: How Fund Regulation Is Organised Internationally
modules.summary: How international standard-setters shape national fund rules, the division of labour between IOSCO and the FSB, and how standards are turned into legislation, rules and guidance at national and regional level.
objectives: Explain the roles of IOSCO, the FSB and the G20 in setting asset management standards
Describe the IOSCO Objectives and Principles relevant to collective investment schemes and managers
Analyse how authorities translate standards into primary law, rules, guidance and supervisory practice
syllabus: The international standard-setting architecture and peer review
IOSCO principles for collective investment schemes and market intermediaries
FSB work on asset management and non-bank financial intermediation
Layers of national and regional rule-making and their interaction

modules.title: Retail, Professional and Alternative Fund Regimes
modules.summary: The two dominant models of fund regulation, product rules for retail funds and manager rules for alternative funds, and the specialist regimes for money market, long-term and venture funds that sit between them.
objectives: Distinguish product-regulated retail funds from manager-regulated alternative fund regimes
Explain eligible asset, diversification, borrowing and concentration rules for retail funds
Assess when a specialist fund label adds investor protection and when it adds complexity
syllabus: Retail fund product rules and the logic of a regulated fund brand
Alternative fund manager regimes: thresholds, registration and private placement
Investor classification: retail, professional and qualifying investor access
Specialist regimes for money market, long-term and venture capital funds

modules.title: Authorising Managers: Governance, Delegation and Substance
modules.summary: What authorities require of fund managers at authorisation and on an ongoing basis, how managers delegate functions while retaining responsibility, and how substance is evidenced and tested.
objectives: Explain fitness, capital, governance, conflicts and remuneration requirements for fund managers
Assess delegation arrangements and the manager's retained oversight of delegates
Identify letter-box risk and how firms evidence substance to supervisors
syllabus: Authorisation criteria: programme of operations, people, capital and resources
Fund governance: boards, independent oversight and conflicts of interest
Delegation of portfolio and risk management and third-country delegates
Substance: senior management, decision-making and the letter-box test

modules.title: Fund Distribution, Suitability and Investor Disclosure
modules.summary: How funds reach investors through advisers, platforms and direct channels, the conduct rules that govern distribution, and the disclosure and costs principles designed to protect investors.
objectives: Explain product governance, target market and distribution oversight obligations
Apply suitability, appropriateness and conflict of interest principles to fund distribution
Assess key investor disclosures and costs and charges from manager to end investor
syllabus: Distribution models: advised, execution-only, platforms and digital channels
Product governance, target market and inducements
Prospectus, key information documents, periodic reports and marketing communications
Costs and charges, performance fees and value for investors

modules.title: Depositaries, Custody and Safeguarding Investor Assets
modules.summary: Why the separation of fund assets from the manager is fundamental to investor protection, the safekeeping and oversight roles of depositaries and custodians, and what happens when safeguarding fails.
objectives: Explain IOSCO standards on the safekeeping and segregation of fund assets
Assess depositary and custodian duties, independence and liability
Evaluate safeguarding arrangements for non-traditional and digital assets
syllabus: Segregation, safekeeping and asset verification across custody chains
Depositary oversight of the manager and cash flow monitoring
Independence, conflicts of interest and liability for loss of assets
Case study: a safeguarding failure and its lessons for investors

modules.title: Liquidity, Leverage and Valuation: The Prudential Toolkit
modules.summary: How international standards address liquidity mismatch, leverage and valuation in funds, the liquidity management tools open-ended funds are expected to have, and the red flags that precede suspensions and losses.
objectives: Explain the FSB and IOSCO recommendations on liquidity mismatch and liquidity management tools
Assess leverage measures, limits and reporting for different fund types
Identify valuation governance weaknesses, especially for hard-to-value assets
syllabus: Liquidity mismatch, stress testing and fund liquidity classification
Anti-dilution tools, gates, notice periods and suspensions
Leverage: the IOSCO framework, gross and commitment measures
Valuation policies, independence and red flags

modules.title: Cross-Border Distribution, Passporting and Mutual Recognition
modules.summary: How funds and managers operate across borders through regional passports, bilateral mutual recognition and private placement, and how home and host authorities share responsibility for investor protection.
objectives: Compare regional fund passports, mutual recognition and private placement routes
Explain home and host responsibilities and supervisory cooperation arrangements
Assess the entry conditions and marketing rules that apply to foreign funds
syllabus: Regional fund passports: design features and conditions for access
Bilateral mutual recognition and equivalence-based arrangements
Private placement, reverse solicitation and pre-marketing
Information sharing, the IOSCO MMoU and host supervision

modules.title: Sustainability Disclosure and Greenwashing Risk
modules.summary: How sustainability-related disclosure applies to funds and managers, from entity-level reporting to product labels and naming conventions, and whether disclosure prevents greenwashing.
objectives: Explain the IOSCO recommendations on sustainability-related practices in asset management
Assess sustainability claims in fund documents, names, labels and marketing
Evaluate disclosure-based and label-based approaches to sustainable fund regulation
syllabus: Entity-level disclosure and the ISSB standards
Product categories, sustainability labels and fund naming rules
Stewardship, engagement and evidencing sustainability outcomes
Break-out: spotting greenwashing and greenbleaching

modules.title: Operational Resilience, Convergence and Emerging Fund Models
modules.summary: Brings the programme together with the cross-cutting rules that reach asset managers, the tools that drive supervisory convergence, and the private market, exchange-traded and tokenised fund models reshaping the sector.
objectives: Explain operational resilience, technology and third-party risk expectations for asset managers
Describe how peer reviews, guidance and supervisory colleges drive convergence
Identify emerging fund models and regulatory topics and agree priorities
syllabus: Operational resilience, cyber risk and critical third-party providers
Private markets, semi-liquid funds and retail access
Exchange-traded funds and tokenised fund units
Workshop: the reform horizon and a twelve-month priorities plan

related.title: EU Asset Management and Investment Fund Regulation (EU Edition)
related.summary: A ten-module programme mapping EU fund and asset management regulation, from UCITS, AIFMD and MiFID II to liquidity, delegation, cross-border marketing, SFDR and DORA.

related.title: Fund Regulation Country Briefings
related.summary: Eleven country webinar briefings on fund vehicles, regulators, authorisation, distribution and recent developments in leading European, offshore and Asia Pacific fund markets.

related.title: International Fund Regulation: Global and Regional Briefings
related.summary: A ten-module webinar series mapping international, EU and Asia Pacific fund regulation and how cross-border fund distribution, management and investment are regulated.

related.title: Introduction to Investment Funds: From Launch to Wind-Down
related.summary: A fourteen-module foundation programme taking new funds professionals and supervisors through every stage of an investment fund, from structure and regulation to operations and wind-down.

related.title: Investment Funds Supervision
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors to oversee investment funds and their managers, from authorisation and valuation to liquidity, leverage, private markets and tokenised funds.

related.title: Fund Governance and Compliance for Managers and Service Providers
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving fund managers and service providers the practical tools to meet fund rules and supervisory expectations across the fund lifecycle.
